title_en: Van wakes up to rain! Here is today's expected weather!
text_en: Van wakes up to rain! Here is today's expected weather! According to data shared by the Meteorological Service, today across the region the sky is expected to be very cloudy, with occasional heavy showers and thunderstorm rain, turning to rain mixed with snow in high areas after the evening hours. Air temperatures are expected to remain below seasonal normals, and winds are forecast to blow from the south and west at moderate speeds, locally strong (50-70 km/h). HEAVY RAIN WARNING The Meteorological Service also issued a heavy rain warning for the region. The warning states: “Since precipitation is expected to be intermittently strong showers and thunderstorm rain at times, care and precaution are required against adverse conditions such as strong winds during rainfall, fallen trees, local hail, lightning strikes, breaks in power transmission lines, flash floods and inundation, traffic delays on highways, waves rising on Lake Van during thunderstorm passages and during strong wind and rain, snowfall on high-altitude mountain passes (Tendürek, Güzeldere, Kurubaş), and reduced visibility.” STRONG WIND WARNING The Meteorological Service also issued a strong wind warning, stating: “Since strong winds (50-70 km/h) are expected in places across the region from the south, care and precaution are required against fallen trees, blown-off roofs, stove and flue gas poisoning, and rising waves on Lake Van during thunderstorm passages and during strong wind and rain.” it said.

title_en: TSMC: Confident in customers; China market restricted, “AI annual growth rate can still reach 40%”
text_en:
TSMC: Confident in customers; China market restricted, “AI annual growth rate can still reach 40%”

▲TSMC. (Photo by reporter Gao Zhaolin)
Reporter Gao Zhaolin / Hsinchu report
Foundry leader TSMC (2330) held its investor conference today. Regarding China's recent rare earth export controls, TSMC said the measures have no direct impact on the company, but it will keep a close watch on them. On China's market restrictions, Chairman Wei Che-chia said the impact on the company is also limited, adding that even if opportunities in China are restricted, he is still confident of achieving the target of an AI market compound annual growth rate of 40% or more.
On recent developments in China, Wei said the restrictions imposed by the United States and by the Chinese government on purchases of US chips are indeed disruptive, but TSMC is very confident in its customers.
Wei explained that the Asian market is performing very well. Even without the China market, he considers AI growth to be very sharp and very positive, so he is confident that customers will keep growing and that TSMC will support them. Therefore, even though opportunities in China are restricted, he is still confident of achieving the AI market compound annual growth rate of 40% or more in the future.

title_en: Fatih Karagümrük did not let Ankaragücü through!
text_en:
Fatih Karagümrük did not let Ankaragücü through! In the week 5 match of the TFF First League, Fatih Karagümrük faced MKE Ankaragücü at home. The match, played at the Atatürk Olympic Stadium, was won 3-2 by the home side. Wesley scored the goals that gave Karagümrük the win in the 4th and 11th minutes, and Lamkel Ze scored in the 82nd minute. The goals for MKE Ankaragücü were scored by Saponara in the 64th minute and Renaldo Cephas in the 84th minute.

2 ASSISTS FROM ÇAĞTAY
Çağtay Kurukalıp, transferred to Karagümrük from Fenerbahçe, made two assists in the match. Baran Demiroğlu, on loan from Galatasaray, came on in the 83rd minute in place of Wesley. Emre Bilgin, on loan to Karagümrük from Beşiktaş, started the match in the number 11 position and stayed on the pitch for 90 minutes.

With this result, Karagümrük raised its points total to 6 and caught up with Ankaragücü, the team it defeated.

In the next league week, Karagümrük will face Şanlıurfaspor. MKE Ankaragücü will host Sakaryaspor.

title_en: Meat price fell 16% in real terms due to lower consumption
text_en: Meat price fell 16% in real terms due to lower consumption In July of this year, the average consumer price of beef was $7,445 per kilo, a 16% decrease in real terms compared with late 2023. According to a report from IERAL of the Fundación Mediterránea, this reduction in the price of beef has played an important role in moderating inflation during the year. The fall in the cost of beef has contributed to an overall decline in inflation, since meat is a significant part of the consumption basket used to calculate price indices. Franco Artusso, author of the report, estimated that the contribution of beef to inflation fell from 2.2 percentage points in December 2023 to just 0.11 points in July 2024 due to the price reduction. Decline in beef consumption Apparent beef consumption, calculated as production minus exports, fell 20% year on year during the first half of the year. This decline is mainly due to the drop in consumers' purchasing power and the contraction of economic activity, which has led to cuts in food spending. As a result, beef consumption has reached historically low levels, reflecting the difficult economic situation of Argentine households. Despite this drop in consumption, the current price of beef remains high compared with the 2007-2023 historical average. To adjust their spending, many families are turning to cheaper alternatives such as chicken and pork, since beef remains relatively expensive. What will determine the future evolution of beef prices? Looking ahead, two major questions arise: will the price of beef keep falling and contribute to the slowdown in prices, or will it start rising again? The answer will depend on several factors, including the evolution of economic activity and the behavior of supply and demand in the market. The fall in meat production during the first seven months of the year, together with a rise in the value of cattle destined for the domestic market, could put upward pressure on prices. In addition, the reduction of tariffs on meat products could raise export prices, adding further pressure on costs in the local market. These factors could lead to an adjustment in beef prices in the coming months, reigniting the economic debate on this topic.
